fields.description:
# `tool_step_limit` empty-filter cutoff 400s on Bedrock/Anthropic — forced landing is provider-broken

## Context / Problem

LIVE-proven (Bedrock us-east-1, haiku-4.5): `build_agent_kwargs` (`src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py:64`)
implements `tool_step_limit` by rewriting toolsets to `.filtered(lambda ctx, _: ctx.run_step <= limit)`.
When the filter trips after any tool call has occurred, pydantic-ai omits `tools`/`toolConfig` from the
next request while the message history still contains `toolUse` blocks. Bedrock Converse rejects that
request: ValidationException 400 "The toolConfig field must be defined when using toolUse and toolResult
content blocks." Anthropic direct has the equivalent documented constraint (tools must be defined when
history contains `tool_use`), and pydantic-ai maps `tool_choice='none'` on Bedrock to omitting
`toolConfig` entirely — the same 400. So the convergence boundary NEVER lands a run that has already
made a tool call — it converts it into a provider error, which `interpret_failure`
(`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:58`) then sweeps into `LLMUnavailableError` ("provider call failed").

Blast radius: every armed site. `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:471` passes
`tool_step_limit=_EVIDENCE_TOOL_STEPS` (16) — the bounded-recovery fallback itself dies with the same
400 if an evidence run reaches step 17.

Why tests miss it: `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` and `tests/unit/test_runner_pydantic_budget.py`
drive the cutoff with `FunctionModel`, which accepts a tools-less request over a `tool_use` history;
the provider protocol constraint is unrepresented offline.

## Approach

Keep the `tool_step_limit` request field and its meaning (a convergence boundary after N run steps) but
change the mechanism from *hiding tools* to *steering with synthetic tool results*: wrap the toolsets in
a `WrapperToolset` subclass whose `call_tool`, once `run_ctx.run_step > limit`, stops executing the tool
and instead returns a fixed steering notice telling the model that tool results are no longer provided
and it must produce its final answer from the evidence already gathered. Tool definitions stay advertised
for the whole run, so the request is always protocol-valid on both first-class providers; nothing raises
mid-protocol; the model lands naturally through the existing output path.

**Terminal backstop — a model that ignores steering cannot spin forever.** Steering is advisory to the
model, so the terminal bound for a non-cooperative model is the one that exists today: `runner.py` sets
`UsageLimits(request_limit=ceil(max_iter/2), tool_calls_limit=max(8, max_iter))` on every run, so a model
that keeps re-issuing tool calls against steered results exhausts that budget and raises
`UsageLimitExceeded` exactly as it does now — steering never weakens the budget, it only adds a graceful
exit before it. (Routing that exhaustion into bounded recovery is [rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911]; tripping
early on the repeat pattern such spinning produces is [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]. This ticket's
obligation is only: steering must not remove or extend the existing budget.)

LIVE-proven end to end: a
deliberately tool-happy agent landed cleanly after 3 real + 7 steered calls, and a structured
`completion_verdict` parsed through the prompted-output path after 4 real + 2 steered calls
(experiments exp_g/exp_h, recorded on [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e] 2026-08-05). This fits the problem
because it is the one shape that keeps the Bedrock/Anthropic constraint satisfied by construction —
industry equivalents (LangChain `early_stopping_method="generate"`, smolagents `provide_final_answer`,
CrewAI `handle_max_iterations_exceeded`) all converge on "stop executing, force a final answer" rather
than "remove the tools"; pydantic-ai itself offers no graceful-landing primitive (issue #2605 open).

`FunctionToolset` and `WrapperToolset` are both importable from `pydantic_ai.toolsets` (confirmed in the
installed pydantic-ai 1.107.1: `pydantic_ai/toolsets/__init__.py` exports both; `WrapperToolset.call_tool`
is the documented override seam). The steering text is a module constant beside the wrapper.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py` — replace the `.filtered()` empty-cutoff branch in `build_agent_kwargs`
  with the steering wrapper; module constant for the steering text.
- `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` — rewrite the cutoff-shape tests to pin the new invariant (tool
  definitions persist past the limit; execution is steered instead).
- `tests/unit/test_runner_pydantic_budget.py` — update the truncation test to assert steering semantics
  through the runner.

Out of scope: the runaway detector and its trip wiring ([rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]); the recovery
catch-miss ([rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911]). `completion_recovery.py:471` needs no edit — it passes
`tool_step_limit` through `RunRequest`, and this ticket fixes what that field does.

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py tests/unit/test_runner_pydantic_budget.py -q

Happy path: a run under the limit executes tools normally and lands its output. Edge: a run that
exceeds the limit gets steering results, keeps its tool definitions advertised on every request, and
still lands. Failure-shape regression: a test asserts that after the limit trips, the toolset still
advertises non-empty tool definitions (the exact condition whose violation produced the 400) — the
assertion is on the request-visible tool surface, not on implementation internals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] no code path empties the advertised tool surface mid-run after a tool call has occurred: a test
      drives a `FunctionModel` run past the limit and asserts every request's tool definitions remain
      non-empty for the whole run
- [ ] past the limit, tool calls are not executed — the tool returns the steering notice instead; a test
      asserts the underlying tool function is not invoked after the limit and the model receives the
      steering text as the tool result
- [ ] a run that exceeds the limit still lands a final output through the normal output path (no
      exception, no empty result); pinned by a `FunctionModel` test whose model calls tools until it
      receives a steering result, then emits its answer
- [ ] a run that never reaches the limit behaves exactly as before: tools execute, output lands; pinned
      by the existing happy-path tests passing (updated only where they asserted the old filtered shape)
- [ ] `tool_step_limit=0` and negative values steer from the first tool call (the existing clamp
      semantics are preserved); verified by a test
- [ ] a steered model that never lands is still terminally bounded: a `FunctionModel` test drives a
      model that keeps issuing tool calls after receiving steering results and asserts the run ends
      with the existing budget exhaustion (`UsageLimitExceeded`-derived failure), not an infinite
      loop — pinning that steering does not remove or extend `UsageLimits`
- [ ] [operator-attested] the steering mechanism is LIVE-proven against the real Bedrock Converse
      boundary: experiments exp_g (tool-happy agent landed cleanly after 3 real + 7 steered calls)
      and exp_h (structured `completion_verdict` parsed after 4 real + 2 steered calls), Bedrock
      us-east-1, recorded as evidence comments on [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e] dated 2026-08-05 —
      the provider-protocol constraint (`toolConfig` must accompany `toolUse` history) is
      unrepresentable under `FunctionModel`, so this live record is the completion check for the
      request-shape validity that the offline ACs cannot carry
- [ ] `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py` still passes: the tool-free finalizer
      (`tool_step_limit is None`, `mode="single_turn"`) is untouched by this change
